subject: Private deployment IaC & CI/CD review for Acme Corp VPC/on-prem
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Bethany Collins <bethany@infra-audit.io>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Oct 2025 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment IaC & CI/CD review for Acme Corp VPC/on-prem

Ravi / Bethany —

Thanks again for the call earlier. As discussed, attaching the initial IaC bundle for the private deployment we plan to run in your VPC-connected colo sites. This thread will be the formal checklist for the review so we can capture action items for SOC2 audit readiness and the procurement/ops handoff.

Attachments included: redwood-acme-terraform.zip (Terraform modules + variables), helm-charts.tar.gz (K8s control-plane & inference charts), acme-network-diagram-v2.png (logical overlay).

High-level asks:
- Can your network team validate the CIDR allocations and transit/peering configuration in the diagram?
- Security review: any procurement constraints for installing customer-managed HSMs or KMS endpoints?
- CI/CD: we propose a two-stage pipeline (lint/plan/test -> gated apply in a restricted service account). We'd like your feedback on pipeline runners (self-hosted in Acme, or Redwood-managed with limited access).

Next steps: please list any gaps we should address before we hand our IaC to your infra team. I propose a follow-up review on Tue 10/21 at 11:00 PT — please confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Bethany Collins <bethany@infra-audit.io>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment IaC & CI/CD review for Acme Corp VPC/on-prem

Marissa —

Got the bundle, thanks. A few quick notes after a skim and forwarding to our network team:

1) Network diagram: the CIDR ranges look fine but we need to reserve an additional /24 for management plane (SSH/metrics) in each colo region. Can you update the Terraform vars so the management_subnet is parameterized (not hardcoded)?

2) Peering/Transit: We operate transit via an overlay (Arista EVPN). The proposed direct VPC peering will need NAT for some legacy services — we'll confirm exact requirements but FYI.

3) HSM/KMS: We'll likely require on-prem HSM for keys in production. Procurement has approved HSM vendor list; I'll attach their vendor matrix separately.

4) CI runners: we prefer self-hosted runners inside our management VLAN for the apply stage. Can you document the minimum host profile and IAM restrictions so our security team can sign off?

For the follow-up, Tue 10/21 11:00 PT works for me.

Ravi
Infrastructure Engineering Lead
Acme Corp

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 12:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment IaC & CI/CD review for Acme Corp VPC/on-prem

Ravi / Marissa —

Thanks — quick technical review notes after pulling the repo and running tf init + plan against a local dev workspace: 

- Terraform modules: we split into 3 top-level modules (network, infra, ops). The network module currently hardcodes the management_subnet in network/main.tf line ~42. I recommend replacing with a variable management_subnet and adding a validation rule so accidental overlap fails early. Example var: management_subnet = { type = string, description = "Reserved management subnet per site" }.

- State management: the repository uses S3 + Dynamo for remote state, with a backend config that assumes an existing bucket named redwood-acme-remote-state. For on-prem/VPC deployments we need an alternative: we suggest offering two backend options in the repo (s3 + local/s3-proxy). Please add a backend.tf template and document the required permissions for the apply-runner service account.

- Helm charts: charts are mostly fine; note that the inference-controller values.yaml enables hostNetwork: true for low-latency networking. That will trigger additional firewall rules — make sure to surface this to network ops.

- CI/CD: Current .gitlab-ci.yml shows a single runner that runs terraform fmt/validate/plan then auto-applies on the main branch. This won't meet Acme's approval. Proposal: convert to a two-pipeline pattern:
  * PR pipeline: fmt/validate/plan + terratest execution (containerized)
  * Release pipeline: gated apply executed by a self-hosted runner in Acme management VLAN, using an assume-role service account limited to apply scope.

- Tests: add a minimal Terratest suite checking that the management_subnet is present and that required IAM roles are present for the runner. I can draft initial tests if you want.

I'll prepare a short diff for the Terraform vars + backend template and bring to the call.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Bethany Collins <bethany@infra-audit.io>

Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment IaC & CI/CD review for Acme Corp VPC/on-prem

Thanks for sharing. A couple of compliance-specific asks prior to the call: 

- Please include a documented runbook for key rotation when HSM is used (who has access, how rotation is audited). This can be a short Markdown file in the repo.
- For Terraform state: we need a proof-of-control for state backend. If you offer S3 + Dynamo, include a sample bucket policy and KMS key policy. If using an s3-proxy/local backend for on-prem, include steps for encrypting state at rest.
- Terratest is great; also include an automated drift detection job (daily plan) that runs against non-prod and emails a topology diff to the security mailbox.

I can review the runbook template after your update.

-Bethany
Principal Auditor, Infra Audit Co.
bethany@infra-audit.io

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment IaC & CI/CD review for Acme Corp VPC/on-prem

Ravi / team —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Confirming we will:
- Parameterize management_subnet and add validation in the network module (Dev: please include the var and a short example in README).
- Add backend.tf template and document S3 vs on-prem options with required IAM perms and sample bucket/KMS policies (Bethany: we'll include this).
- Swap the single apply runner for a two-stage pipeline with self-hosted apply runner in Acme's management VLAN. We'll provide a minimal host profile and assume-role example.

Marissa — please coordinate procurement & onboarding collateral for the HSM vendor list Ravi mentioned. Also confirm who from Acme will own the self-hosted runner setup (point person + schedule).

I'll join the Tue 11:00 PT call for the final sign-off.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com
